School of Artificial Intelligence, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Быстрее говорить, сохраняя качество: разделяем токены генерации и синтеза речи
ru.desc: Статья предлагает CoSTA — пост-хок фреймворк, который разделяет пространства токенов для генерации и синтеза речи в Spoken Dialogue Models. Генерация работает с сжатыми представлениями, расширяя словарь через mean-initialized vocabulary extension, адаптацию произношения и адаптацию диалога. Перед синтезом сжатые токены детерминированно разворачиваются обратно в исходное пространство речевых токенов, поэтому оригинальный токенизатор и декодер сохраняются. Эксперименты на двуязычных речевых диалоговых бенчмарках показывают примерно 1.7-кратное ускорение генерации, снижение задержки и рост пропускной способности без потери качества ответов.

en.title: Decoupling for Faster and Better Spoken Dialogue Models
en.desc: The paper introduces CoSTA, a framework designed to improve the efficiency of spoken dialogue models (SDMs) by separating the generation and synthesis token spaces. Traditional SDMs often face challenges with long autoregressive sequences and high inference costs due to their shared speech-token space. CoSTA enhances the generation process by using compressed representations while maintaining compatibility with existing speech tokenizers and decoders. The results show that CoSTA significantly speeds up speech-token generation and reduces latency, all while ensuring high-quality responses in bilingual speech-dialogue tasks.

zh.title: CoSTA：加速语音对话模型的创新框架
zh.desc: CoSTA是一种新框架，它将生成和合成的令牌空间分开，从而加速语音对话模型，同时保持质量和兼容性。传统的语音对话模型通常共享一个令牌空间，这导致生成过程较长且推理成本高。CoSTA通过扩展生成令牌空间，使用压缩表示来提高生成速度，并在合成前将其转换回原始的语音令牌空间。实验表明，CoSTA在双语语音对话基准测试中实现了约1.7倍的生成速度提升，同时保持了响应质量。

papers.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
papers.abstract: Abstract WebAnything automates the reconstruction of reusable, source-grounded web environments from real URLs, enabling scalable agent training and evaluation with verified fidelity.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. Human-assisted mirrors demand per-site engineering, while generative construction can diverge from specified real websites. Capture-and-replay preserves observations, with interaction coverage constrained by captured content and replay capabilities.   We present WebAnything, a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable Web environments from real URLs without per-site manual implementation or repair after initial setup and authorization. An Explorer-Builder collects browser-observable structures, resources, and interaction outcomes; an independent verifier checks frozen candidates and guides local repair or targeted source recapture.   We construct 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. Compared with human-assisted WebHarbor, WebAnything achieves higher aggregate scores on three fidelity metrics, with 12 wins, two ties, and no losses in a blind audit. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories improves REAL success by 9.9 percentage points, Odysseys-Easy Rubric Avg and Task Avg by 6.25 and 6.32 percentage points, and WebArena-Verified Overall success by 13.33 percentage points under the fixed harness. Code: https://github.com/china-qijizhifeng/Web-Anything

ru.title: Реальные сайты по ссылке, автоматически превращённые в среды для обучения AI-агентов
ru.desc: В статье представлен WebAnything — полностью автоматизированный фреймворк, который восстанавливает пригодные для повторного использования веб-среды по реальным URL без ручной настройки под каждый сайт. Система использует Explorer-Builder для сбора структур, ресурсов и результатов взаимодействий в браузере, а независимый верификатор проверяет готовые кандидаты и при необходимости запускает локальное исправление или целевую перезапись источника. Построено 244 артефакта сайтов в 14 доменах, на которых выполнено 12 984 принятых задачи, и по метрикам точности WebAnything превосходит human-assisted WebHarbor. Дообучение Qwen3.5-9B на 5 856 траекториях взаимодействий улучшает результаты на REAL, Odysseys-Easy и WebArena-Verified, что подтверждает пользу таких сред для обучения и оценки AI-агентов.

en.title: Automating Web Environment Reconstruction for Scalable Agent Training
en.desc: WebAnything is a framework that automates the creation of reusable web environments from real URLs, which helps in training and evaluating agents effectively. It eliminates the need for manual setup by using an Explorer-Builder to gather necessary web structures and resources, while an independent verifier ensures the accuracy of these environments. The system has successfully generated 244 website artifacts across various domains, allowing for extensive testing with nearly 13,000 tasks executed. Compared to traditional methods, WebAnything shows significant improvements in fidelity metrics, demonstrating its efficiency and reliability in agent training.

zh.title: WebAnything：自动化重建网站环境的创新框架
zh.desc: WebAnything 是一个自动化框架，可以从真实的 URL 重建可重用的、基于源的网站环境，支持可扩展的智能体训练和评估。该框架通过 Explorer-Builder 收集浏览器可观察的结构和资源，并由独立的验证器检查生成的候选网站。与人工辅助的 WebHarbor 相比，WebAnything 在三个保真度指标上取得了更高的综合得分。通过对 Qwen3.5-9B 进行微调，显著提高了任务成功率和评估指标。

papers.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
papers.abstract: Abstract Glance integrates reranking and generation into a single backbone using lightweight adapters and pointer heads to score passages from shared context, reducing memory overhead while improving retrieval and answer quality.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Retrieval-augmented generation commonly serves separate models for reranking and answering, duplicating model residency and passage processing. We introduce Glance, which equips the generator with a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head to score candidate passages from a shared prefill. Short relevance probes branch from the cached context, producing one score per passage without separately prefilling each query-passage pair. A single resident 9B backbone supports generation, general decisions and reranking, with approximately 0.1 GiB of additional memory per decision skill. After 39 minutes of MS MARCO fine-tuning, Glance achieves nDCG@10 of 0.741 on SciFact and 0.345 on NFCorpus, compared with 0.721 and 0.326 for bge-reranker-v2-m3. On 300 HotpotQA questions, its selected context improves answer F1 by 0.045 over cross-encoder-selected context under the same base generator (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.014, 0.076]). In a scaling study, reranking quality keeps rising up to 200 candidates (43k tokens) scored from one shared prefill, where it exceeds the cross-encoder by 0.058 nDCG@10, and a probe-only activated adapter lets generation continue from the original passage cache. These initial results demonstrate generator-based reranking with one resident backbone; evaluation currently covers two retrieval datasets, one QA dataset and one backbone family.

ru.title: Один backbone для поиска и генерации ответов
ru.desc: Статья представляет Glance — подход, который объединяет переранжирование и генерацию ответов в одной языковой модели (LLM) с помощью лёгких адаптеров и pointer head. Модель оценивает кандидатные пассажи по общему кэшу контекста, поэтому не нужно отдельно обрабатывать каждую пару запрос-пассаж, что снижает потребление памяти. Такой подход на бенчмарках SciFact, NFCorpus и HotpotQA даёт лучшее качество поиска и ответов, чем отдельные cross-encoder модели. Авторы отмечают, что эксперименты пока ограничены двумя наборами данных для поиска, одним QA-датасетом и одним семейством моделей.

en.title: Glance: Unified Reranking and Generation for Efficient Retrieval
en.desc: The paper introduces Glance, a novel approach that combines reranking and generation in a single model architecture, which reduces memory usage while enhancing the quality of retrieval and answers. By utilizing lightweight adapters and pointer heads, Glance efficiently scores candidate passages from a shared context without the need for separate model instances for reranking and answering. This method allows for improved performance on various datasets, achieving higher nDCG scores and better answer quality compared to existing models. The results indicate that Glance can effectively handle multiple tasks with a single backbone, demonstrating its potential for scalable retrieval-augmented generation applications.

zh.title: Glance：高效整合重排序与生成的模型
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为Glance的模型，它将重排序和生成整合到一个轻量级的框架中。通过使用轻量级适配器和指针头，Glance能够从共享上下文中对候选段落进行评分，从而减少内存开销并提高检索和回答的质量。与传统的分开模型不同，Glance通过共享的预填充来处理查询-段落对，显著提高了效率。实验结果表明，Glance在多个数据集上表现优异，尤其是在重排序质量和答案准确性方面。

papers.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right
papers.abstract: Abstract Soft-MTP removes a noisy gradient residual from multi-token prediction via a straight-through KL recovery trick, improving perplexity, speculative decoding, and reasoning without added cost.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) is now a common ingredient in language-model pre-training, as it improves downstream performance and enables faster inference through speculative decoding. We identify a flaw in standard MTP training, in which a residual component of the MTP gradient interferes with both next-token and multi-token learning, increasingly so with scale. Specifically, the MTP cross-entropy gradient can be decomposed exactly into a KL self-distillation term that pulls each MTP head toward the model's own next-token prediction (NTP) distribution and improves speculative decoding, and a residual that has a low signal-to-noise ratio and buries the useful KL signal. We introduce the KL gradient-recovery trick: when two distributions share a linear output head, the gradient of their KL divergence can be recovered exactly by combining their cross-entropy gradients through straight-through gradient routing. Unlike minimizing the KL directly, this trick requires no vocabulary-sized logit matrices and is compatible with standard fused cross-entropy kernels. This enables Soft Multi-Token Prediction (Soft-MTP), a one-line code change to MTP that removes the noisy residual and backpropagates only the KL self-distillation signal by reusing the existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy computations. Soft-MTP supports both DeepSeek- and Meta-style MTP, adds no parameters, and incurs no measurable overhead. From 167M to 1.2B parameters, Soft-MTP improves over standard MTP with lower NTP perplexity, faster speculative decoding and higher zero-shot accuracy at every scale, lower MTP perplexity from 689M onward, and stronger math and code reasoning after fine-tuning at 1.2B. Soft-MTP also matches, if not exceeds, direct KL divergence minimization on most metrics. Soft-MTP is, in effect, a free lunch for MTP optimization. Our code can be found at https://github.com/JaydenTeoh/Soft-MTP.

ru.title: Убери шум из MTP — и модель станет быстрее и умнее бесплатно
ru.desc: В статье обнаружен недостаток стандартного обучения Multi-Token Prediction (MTP): часть градиента cross-entropy мешает как обучению предсказания следующего токена, так и многотокенного предсказания, и этот эффект усиливается с ростом масштаба модели. Авторы показывают, что градиент MTP раскладывается на KL self-distillation, полезный для speculative decoding, и шумный остаточный член с низким signal-to-noise ratio. Предложенный трюк KL gradient-recovery через straight-through gradient routing позволяет получить градиент KL-дивергенции без больших матриц логитов, а метод Soft-MTP реализуется одной строкой кода. Эксперименты от 167M до 1.2B параметров показывают улучшение perplexity, скорости speculative decoding и точности без дополнительных параметров и накладных расходов.

en.title: Soft-MTP: A Free Lunch for Multi-Token Prediction Optimization
en.desc: The paper introduces Soft-Multi-Token Prediction (Soft-MTP), a method that enhances multi-token prediction in language models by addressing a noisy gradient issue. It utilizes a KL gradient-recovery trick to improve the training process without increasing computational costs. By effectively removing the residual noise from the gradient, Soft-MTP allows for better next-token and multi-token learning, leading to improved performance metrics such as perplexity and reasoning capabilities. This approach is efficient, requiring only a simple code modification and no additional parameters, making it a valuable optimization for large-scale models.

zh.title: Soft-MTP：多标记预测的优化新方法
zh.desc: Soft-MTP是一种改进的多标记预测方法，通过KL恢复技巧去除噪声梯度残差，从而提高了模型的困惑度、推测解码和推理能力，而无需增加额外的计算成本。传统的多标记预测训练存在缺陷，残差成分会干扰下一个标记和多标记的学习。我们提出的KL梯度恢复技巧可以通过直通梯度路由精确恢复KL散度的梯度，避免了直接最小化KL所需的复杂计算。Soft-MTP在不同参数规模下均表现出更低的困惑度和更快的推测解码速度，是多标记预测优化的有效方法。

papers.title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?
papers.abstract: Abstract Investor's Last Exam evaluates financial agents on end-to-end equity research using frozen evidence, expert criteria, and dependency graphs, revealing that top models excel at research but fail at forecasting and investment judgments.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Financial agents must form forecasts and investment judgments from decision-time evidence, with predictions evaluated against subsequent outcomes. Existing benchmarks assess financial knowledge, research workflows, or forecasting, but evaluating the full research process requires a strictly frozen information set and professional evaluation criteria. We introduce Investor's Last Exam (ILE), an equity-research benchmark led by experienced buy-side investors and fund managers. Its three components are a versioned financial database spanning 3.43 million document versions and nine source categories, supplemented by structured market data, with validated timestamps governing retrieval and computation; a task taxonomy organized around professional analyst deliverables; and an expert-led framework linking scoring criteria to sources, calculations, and assumptions through financial dependency graphs. Evaluation spans 86 assignments and jointly assesses research quality, forecast accuracy, and simulated investment performance. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 lead overall at 68.1 and 66.9 out of 100, yet even Astra scores only 52.5 on Forecast & Model. Our results show that even state-of-the-art models fail to translate overall research capability into predictive performance. ILE shifts the evaluation unit from isolated capabilities to the evidence--assumption--judgment chain, allowing researchers to locate where analytical advantages fail to translate into forecasts and investment judgments, and providing a traceable, diagnostic foundation for training and evaluating financial agents.
affiliations: Antai College of Economics and Management, SJTU

ru.title: Хорошо исследуешь — не значит хорошо прогнозируешь
ru.desc: В статье представлен Investor's Last Exam (ILE) — бенчмарк для оценки финансовых агентов на полном цикле equity research, созданный под руководством опытных buy-side инвесторов. Агенты получают «замороженный» набор данных с проверенными временными метками, включающий более 3,43 млн версий документов из девяти категорий источников, и должны формировать прогнозы и инвестиционные решения. Оценка проводится по 86 заданиям с использованием финансовых графов зависимостей, связывающих критерии оценки с источниками, расчётами и допущениями. Результаты показывают, что даже лучшие LLM хорошо справляются с исследованием, но проваливаются в прогнозировании и инвестиционных суждениях, например, лучшая модель набирает лишь 52,5 балла из 100 по Forecast & Model.

en.title: Bridging Research Excellence and Predictive Performance in Finance
en.desc: The paper introduces Investor's Last Exam (ILE), a benchmark designed to evaluate financial agents on their ability to conduct comprehensive equity research. It highlights that while top machine learning models excel in research tasks, they struggle with making accurate forecasts and investment decisions. The ILE framework includes a vast financial database, a structured task taxonomy, and expert evaluation criteria, all aimed at assessing the entire research process rather than isolated capabilities. This approach allows for a deeper understanding of where analytical strengths do not translate into effective predictions and investment judgments.

zh.title: 投资者最后考试：揭示金融研究与预测的差距
zh.desc: 本文介绍了投资者最后考试（ILE），这是一个评估金融代理在股票研究中的表现的基准。研究表明，尽管顶尖模型在研究方面表现出色，但在预测和投资判断上却存在不足。ILE通过使用冻结的信息集和专业评估标准，全面评估研究质量、预测准确性和模拟投资表现。该基准的设计帮助研究人员识别分析优势未能转化为预测和投资判断的环节，从而为金融代理的训练和评估提供了可追溯的基础。

papers.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Abstract Proactive video understanding should include asking for missing information under uncertainty, and the AskStream benchmark reveals current models struggle with this decision.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. The evolution from offline to streaming and proactive interaction has gradually shifted models from passive responders toward more proactive agents that can decide when to answer. However, existing proactive paradigms typically assume that the information required to answer a query is complete, leaving models to only wait or answer. In the real world, however, information is often incomplete due to uncertainty from either the video or the user. In proactive paradigms, such uncertainty can cause the model to wait forever or generate highly hallucinatory responses. We therefore argue that proactive interaction should be redefined with a third action: ask, allowing models to actively ask for missing information. To study when and what models should ask before answering, we introduce AskStream, the first multi-turn benchmark spanning video and user uncertainty for streaming video understanding, with four task categories and eight subtasks. It contains 438 videos with 2,714 manually annotated frame-level time windows across three types: wait, ask, and answer. Across both multiple-choice and open-ended settings, even the strongest model attains only 52.18% on our proposed Ask-F1 metric, highlighting substantial limitations in proactive information seeking under uncertainty.
affiliations: Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI), Beijing, China
Minzu University of China, Beijing, China
The Key Laboratory of Cognition and Decision Intelligence for Complex Systems, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China

ru.title: Модели должны уметь спрашивать, а не только отвечать
ru.desc: Статья вводит AskStream — первый многоходовой бенчмарк для потоковой обработки видео, где модели должны решать, ждать, спрашивать или отвечать. Авторы показывают, что существующие мультимодальные LLM рассчитывают на полную информацию и поэтому либо зависают в ожидании, либо галлюцинируют. Предлагается третье действие — ask, позволяющее модели активно запрашивать недостающие данные у пользователя. Лучшая из протестированных моделей достигает лишь 52.18% по метрике Ask-F1, что указывает на серьезные ограничения в проактивном поиске информации при неопределенности.

en.title: Empowering Video Understanding: Ask Before Answering!
en.desc: This paper discusses the need for proactive video understanding systems to ask for missing information when faced with uncertainty. Current models often assume they have all the necessary information to respond, which can lead to delays or incorrect answers. The authors introduce the AskStream benchmark, which evaluates how well models can decide when to ask for more information before providing an answer. Their findings reveal that even advanced models struggle with this task, achieving only 52.18% on the Ask-F1 metric, indicating significant room for improvement in proactive interaction under uncertainty.

zh.title: 主动视频理解：在不确定性中主动询问
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了主动视频理解中的不确定性问题，提出了在缺失信息时模型应该主动询问的概念。现有的主动交互模型通常假设回答问题所需的信息是完整的，但在现实中，信息往往是不完整的。为了解决这个问题，论文引入了AskStream基准，旨在研究模型在回答之前应该何时以及询问什么信息。通过这个基准，研究者希望提高模型在不确定性下的主动信息获取能力。

papers.title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing
papers.abstract: Abstract EditAgent broadens agentic image editing by routing steps to diverse editors and using verification records for listwise judging, improving reliability and efficiency.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Agentic image editors decompose complex requests into steps, but when a step fails, they mostly retry with the same narrow set of tools and a judge that scores each output by eye directly. We argue that such agents are bounded by two spaces: the action space of what the agent can do, and the observation space of what its judge can see. On our expert-annotated benchmark, a general-purpose editor yields no usable result in over 40% of the cases, and no judge is reliable across edit types. We present EditAgent, which expands both spaces. It routes each step to general editors and specialized methods, and attaches to each candidate a verification record. With these records, off-the-shelf VLM judges outperform finetuned reward models. Candidates are generated in parallel and judged in one listwise call: experts prefer this to sequential refinement in 78.5% of decided comparisons, at no more than half the judge calls. EditAgent improves two open-weight editors on three benchmarks and serves as a data engine for training stronger editors.

ru.title: Расширяем действия и зрение агента — надёжнее редактирование изображений
ru.desc: Статья представляет EditAgent — агентную систему для редактирования изображений, которая расширяет пространство действий, направляя каждый шаг к разным редакторам, включая специализированные методы. Каждому кандидату прикрепляется запись верификации, что позволяет готовым VLM-судьям превосходить дообученные reward-модели. Кандидаты генерируются параллельно и оцениваются одним listwise-вызовом, что эксперты предпочитают последовательному уточнению в 78.5% случаев при вдвое меньшем числе вызовов судьи. Система улучшает два open-weight редактора на трёх бенчмарках и служит источником данных для обучения более сильных редакторов.

en.title: Expanding the Horizons of Image Editing with EditAgent
en.desc: EditAgent enhances the process of agentic image editing by directing tasks to various specialized editors and utilizing verification records for better evaluation. Traditional agents often retry failed steps with limited tools, leading to inefficiencies and unreliable outcomes. This paper identifies the constraints of action and observation spaces that hinder performance and proposes a solution that expands these spaces. By generating candidates in parallel and using verification records, EditAgent significantly improves the reliability of image editing results and reduces the number of evaluations needed.

zh.title: EditAgent：提升图像编辑的可靠性与效率
zh.desc: EditAgent 是一种新的图像编辑方法，它通过将编辑步骤分配给不同的编辑器，并使用验证记录来提高编辑的可靠性和效率。传统的编辑器在处理复杂请求时，往往会在失败后重复使用相同的工具，导致结果不理想。EditAgent 扩展了编辑器的操作空间和观察空间，使每个步骤可以使用更广泛的编辑方法，并为每个候选结果附加验证记录。通过这种方式，EditAgent 在多个基准测试中显著提高了编辑效果，并为训练更强大的编辑器提供了数据支持。

papers.title: PhysInsert: Physically Plausible Object Insertion with Geometric Priors and Bidirectional Object-Scene Interactions
papers.abstract: Abstract PhysInsert enables physically plausible object insertion by jointly adapting objects and scenes using geometry-guided adaptation and spatial supervision on aligned counterfactual data.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present PhysInsert, a framework for physically plausible reference-based object insertion that jointly adapts objects and their surrounding scenes. Existing methods often rely on masked inputs, generation-based pairs, or training pairs with limited viewpoint variation, leaving pose and illumination adaptation and bidirectional object-scene interactions insufficiently constrained. We construct the Insert World dataset with strictly aligned Blender-rendered counterfactual pairs and object references across viewpoints and lighting conditions. Building on these data, Geometry-Guided Adaptation couples a VGGT geometry stream with image and text streams under target-scene feature supervision to guide spatially consistent insertion. Complementary 2D Object-Scene Spatial Supervision jointly supervises object occupancy and environmental changes while grounding spatial instructions in object regions through image-text attention. We introduce PhysInsert-Bench with dedicated cross-environment and cross-view cases requiring illumination and pose adaptation beyond appearance copying. Experiments on PhysInsert-Bench and DreamBooth demonstrate improved image fidelity; a user study further shows more accurate placement and improved lighting integration, perspective, and pose plausibility.
affiliations: School of Computer Science and Engineering, Beihang University

ru.title: Вставляем объект так, чтобы он физически вписывался в сцену
ru.desc: PhysInsert — это фреймворк для вставки объектов по референсу, который физически правдоподобно адаптирует и сам объект, и окружающую сцену. Авторы строят датасет Insert World с точно выровненными контрфактуальными парами, отрендеренными в Blender, при разных ракурсах и освещении. Модуль Geometry-Guided Adaptation объединяет геометрический поток VGGT с потоками изображения и текста, а 2D Object-Scene Spatial Supervision контролирует занятость объекта и изменения окружения. Эксперименты на PhysInsert-Bench и DreamBooth подтверждают улучшение точности изображения, а пользовательское исследование показывает более корректное освещение, перспективу и позу объекта.

en.title: Realistic Object Insertion Made Possible!
en.desc: PhysInsert is a framework designed for inserting objects into scenes in a way that looks realistic and physically plausible. It uses a combination of geometry-guided adaptation and spatial supervision to ensure that both the objects and the scenes are adjusted appropriately. The method addresses limitations of previous techniques by utilizing a specially constructed dataset that includes aligned images under various lighting and viewpoint conditions. Experiments show that PhysInsert improves the quality of image generation, making object placement more accurate and enhancing the integration of lighting and perspective.

zh.title: 物理合理的物体插入框架
zh.desc: PhysInsert 是一个框架，旨在通过几何引导适应和空间监督，实现物体与场景的物理上合理插入。该方法利用严格对齐的 Blender 渲染的反事实数据集，解决了现有方法在姿态和光照适应方面的不足。通过几何引导适应，结合图像和文本流，确保插入过程的空间一致性。同时，2D 物体-场景空间监督共同监督物体占用和环境变化，提高了插入的准确性和光照整合效果。

papers.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
papers.abstract: Abstract An online reinforcement learning framework trains UI navigation agents on live mobile apps using a planning agent, UI grounding model, and a novel neighbor-conditioned value estimation method to improve robustness and reduce inference costs.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use. Conversely, smaller models trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or offline reinforcement learning often memorize static trajectories, leading to brittle execution and an inability to recover from errors. To address these limitations, we propose a novel online reinforcement learning framework that trains UI navigation agents directly on live iOS applications. Our framework decouples the agent into two specialized components: a Planning agent and a UI Grounding model. We rely on an LLM-as-a-Judge to provide comprehensive reward signals, combining dense, step-level feedback to evaluate intermediate progress with a terminal reward for overall task completion. To effectively leverage this dual reward structure, we optimize the agent using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with step-level advantage estimation. Furthermore, we introduce GiGPPO, a novel neighbor-conditioned value estimation method that improves critic stability by leveraging reward signals from visually similar states across concurrent trajectories. To support this online training paradigm at scale, we introduce an efficient infrastructure that orchestrates hundreds of concurrent virtual iOS devices. Evaluations on rigorous benchmarks, including UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld, demonstrate that our online RL trained agents substantially outperform both SFT and terminal-only RL baselines while accelerating training convergence. Notably, our 8B RL agents achieve nearly a sevenfold improvement over the SFT baseline in out-of-distribution generalization to Android environments, while outperforming Gemini-3.5-Flash and tying with Gemini-3.1-Pro on real iOS applications.

ru.title: Учимся навигировать по приложениям на живых устройствах, а не по запомненным траекториям
ru.desc: Статья предлагает онлайн-фреймворк обучения с подкреплением для агентов, которые навигируют по интерфейсам мобильных приложений, разделяя агента на Planning agent и UI Grounding model. Вместо offline RL или SFT, которые приводят к запоминанию траекторий, агенты обучаются на живых iOS-приложениях с помощью PPO, а награда формируется LLM-as-a-Judge: плотные пошаговые сигналы плюс терминальная награда. Ключевой вклад — GiGPPO, метод оценки value с учётом соседних визуально похожих состояний из параллельных траекторий, что стабилизирует critic. Восьмимиллиардные RL-агенты заметно превосходят SFT-базовые модели и хорошо обобщаются на Android, сопоставимы с крупными моделями Gemini на iOS.

en.title: Revolutionizing UI Navigation with Online Reinforcement Learning
en.desc: This paper presents an innovative online reinforcement learning framework designed to train UI navigation agents on live mobile applications. It introduces a Planning agent and a UI Grounding model to enhance the robustness of navigation while minimizing inference costs. The framework utilizes a dual reward structure, combining detailed feedback with a final reward, and employs Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for optimization. Additionally, the novel neighbor-conditioned value estimation method, GiGPPO, improves stability by using reward signals from similar states, leading to significant performance gains over traditional training methods.

zh.title: 在线强化学习提升UI导航代理的效率与稳定性
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种在线强化学习框架，用于在实时移动应用中训练用户界面（UI）导航代理。该框架将代理分为两个专门组件：规划代理和UI基础模型，并利用大型语言模型（LLM）提供全面的奖励信号。通过使用近端策略优化（PPO）和新颖的邻居条件价值估计方法（GiGPPO），该方法提高了代理的稳定性和训练效率。实验结果表明，在线强化学习训练的代理在多个基准测试中显著优于传统的监督微调和终端奖励强化学习基线。

papers.title: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation
papers.abstract: Abstract OpenFlyV2 is a unified onboard vision-language-action model that enables real-time aerial navigation and reasoning on resource-constrained hardware using shared multimodal representations.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Human cognition flexibly draws on a shared perceptual foundation to understand environments, attend to referenced entities, reason about spatial relationships, and act. Endowing aerial robots with an analogous functional organization remains challenging, as existing systems are often specialized for individual capabilities, dependent on offboard computation, or unable to sustain closed-loop operation on resource-constrained platforms. We present OpenFlyV2, a unified onboard vision-language-action architecture that uses a shared vision-language representation to support semantic understanding, language-grounded perception, spatial reasoning, and continuous aerial control within a single model. A compact action expert converts the shared multimodal context into short-horizon flight waypoints, while motion-aware temporal memory and action priors reduce the computational cost of closed-loop execution. We construct , a simulation-based dataset comprising approximately 70,000 navigation trajectories and 60,000 vision-language instruction--response pairs. OpenFlyV2 generates action chunks, each comprising 12 waypoints, entirely onboard at 10 Hz using an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX. It transfers zero-shot from simulation to physical quadrotor flight, achieving a 48\% navigation success rate across four real-world environments without real-world aerial training data. Extensive results demonstrate that broad vision-language competence and continuous closed-loop flight can coexist within a single model on a resource-constrained aerial platform. Code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Ideal-ljl/AeroBrain.

University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Единый мозг дрона: язык, зрение и полёт в одной модели на борту
ru.desc: Статья представляет OpenFlyV2 — унифицированную vision-language-action модель, которая работает прямо на борту дрона и управляет полётом в реальном времени. Единое мультимодальное представление позволяет решать задачи семантического понимания, языковой привязки восприятия, пространственного рассуждения и непрерывного управления без внешних вычислений. Компактный action expert генерирует короткие траектории из 12 путевых точек с частотой 10 Гц на NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, а temporal memory и action priors снижают вычислительные затраты. Модель обучена на симуляционном датасете из около 70 тысяч траекторий и 60 тысяч пар инструкция-ответ и переносится на реальный квадрокоптер zero-shot, достигая 48% успешной навигации без реальных данных для воздушного обучения.

en.title: Unified Vision-Language-Action for Aerial Navigation
en.desc: OpenFlyV2 is an advanced model designed for aerial robots that combines vision, language, and action into one system, allowing it to navigate and make decisions in real-time. It uses a shared multimodal representation to understand its surroundings, interpret language instructions, and perform spatial reasoning, all while operating on limited hardware resources. The model can generate flight paths and execute them efficiently without relying on external computing power, making it suitable for closed-loop operations. By training on a large dataset of navigation scenarios, OpenFlyV2 demonstrates impressive performance in real-world environments, achieving a notable success rate without prior physical training.

zh.title: 统一的空中导航与推理模型
zh.desc: OpenFlyV2是一种统一的机载视觉-语言-动作模型，能够在资源受限的硬件上实现实时的空中导航和推理。该模型通过共享的多模态表示，支持语义理解、语言基础的感知、空间推理和连续的空中控制。与现有系统不同，OpenFlyV2能够在单一模型中实现广泛的视觉-语言能力和闭环飞行控制，且无需依赖离线计算。通过构建一个包含约70,000条导航轨迹和60,000对视觉-语言指令响应的数据集，OpenFlyV2在真实环境中实现了48%的导航成功率。

papers.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Abstract AB-Attention approximates dense video diffusion attention with high sparsity via intra-block clustering, weighted sampling, and fine-grained kernel gathering, improving fidelity and speed.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Video diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos, but the quadratic cost of 3D full attention dominates their inference. Dynamic block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing exact attention only on key/value blocks selected from current activations. However, its fidelity degrades under aggressive sparsity: blocks are scored from coarse summaries or formed by costly global clustering, pruned blocks vanish from the softmax, and whole tiles are kept or dropped even when only a few of their keys matter. To address these limitations, we propose Accurate Block Attention (AB-Attention), a training-free method that accurately approximates dense attention at high sparsity. Its Intra-Block Clustering Selector (IBCS) estimates block importance faithfully yet cheaply by clustering queries only within each query block, without permuting tokens. Sampling with Inclusion-Probability Weighting (SIP) then samples blocks in proportion to these estimates and reweights them by inverse inclusion probability, so that one pass estimates dense attention rather than truncating it. Finally, its kernel gathers key/value blocks much smaller than a tile into full tensor-core tiles, refining selection at no extra tensor-core cost. On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, AB-Attention skips 89--92\% of attention, whereas the baselines compute 1.8--3.6times as much, yet it still improves PSNR by up to 4.4~dB over the strongest baseline and achieves up to 2.23times end-to-end speedup. Our code is available at https://github.com/InfRec-Cardinal/AB-Attention.

The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Быстрое внимание для видео без потери качества
ru.desc: Статья предлагает AB-Attention — метод без дообучения, который приближает плотное внимание (dense attention) в диффузионных трансформерах для генерации видео с высокой разреженностью. Ключевые компоненты: IBCS оценивает важность блоков через кластеризацию запросов внутри каждого блока, а SIP выбирает блоки с вероятностями включения и применяет обратное взвешивание, чтобы оценка оставалась несмещённой. Ядро (kernel) собирает небольшие key/value блоки в полные тензорные тайлы, уточняя выбор без дополнительных затрат на tensor cores. На моделях Wan2.1 и HunyuanVideo метод пропускает 89–92% вычислений внимания, повышает PSNR до 4.4 dB и ускоряет inference до 2.23 раза.

en.title: Efficient Video Attention with High Fidelity
en.desc: The paper introduces Accurate Block Attention (AB-Attention), a method designed to enhance the efficiency of video diffusion transformers by approximating dense attention with high sparsity. It utilizes intra-block clustering to accurately assess the importance of key/value blocks, allowing for effective sampling without the need for complex global clustering. By employing Inclusion-Probability Weighting, AB-Attention ensures that the sampled blocks maintain fidelity while significantly reducing computational costs. The results demonstrate that AB-Attention can skip up to 92% of attention calculations while improving video quality and achieving faster processing speeds compared to existing methods.

zh.title: 高效视频生成的精准注意力机制
zh.desc: AB-Attention是一种新方法，通过内部块聚类、加权采样和细粒度核聚合，在高稀疏性下准确近似密集视频扩散注意力，从而提高了视频生成的保真度和速度。传统的3D全注意力计算成本较高，而动态块稀疏注意力通过仅计算选定的关键/值块来降低这一成本。AB-Attention通过在每个查询块内聚类来准确评估块的重要性，并通过包含概率加权进行采样，从而避免了传统方法中的信息丢失。实验结果表明，AB-Attention在保持高质量视频生成的同时，显著提高了计算效率和速度。

papers.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
papers.abstract: Abstract A simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation on low-cost robot arms reveals that hybrid LLM agents outperform learned vision-language-action policies, with ranking consistency between simulation and real hardware.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Low-cost arms such as the SO-101 have become the most common entry point to robot learning, yet no released policy performs spatially constrained, language-conditioned tasks on them out of the box, and existing SO-101 benchmarks run only on physical hardware with simple tasks and few held-out objects. We introduce SO-101 Bench, a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a real SO-101 setup. It has four tasks scored as five families, 138 objects in seen, unseen-instance and unseen-class splits, 916 evaluation episodes with subsets for held-out appearances, rotate-to-fit planning and occlusion memory, and 3,629 simulated demonstrations on which every learned policy is fine-tuned under an equal compute budget. The twin ranks policies as the real robot does: five policies trained without real data, four VLAs and an LLM agent, keep their exact ranking when the same weights run on the physical arm in an unseen environment with unseen objects (Spearman rho = 1.00, MMRV = 0.000), although simulation overestimates success. Across nine VLAs and world-action models, the best learned policies score near 61%, with spatial placement, unseen object classes and rotate-to-fit planning remaining open. An LLM agent that writes code and hands grasping to a learned policy scores 83.2%, and an ablation shows that this lead comes from the choice of harness and the choice of language model.
affiliations: National Institute for Health and Welfare (THL)

ru.title: Симуляция, которой можно доверять: честно ранжируем роботов до их покупки
ru.desc: Статья представляет SO-101 Bench — симулированный бенчмарк для языково-обусловленной пространственной манипуляции на недорогих роботических руках SO-101, построенный на цифровом двойнике в Isaac Lab. Бенчмарк включает 916 эпизодов оценки, 138 объектов и 3 629 демонстраций для дообучения политик (VLA и world-action models) при равном вычислительном бюджете. Показано, что ранжирование политик в симуляции полностью совпадает с реальным роботом (Spearman rho = 1.00), хотя симуляция несколько завышает успешность. Лучшие обученные VLA достигают около 61%, тогда как гибридный LLM-агент, пишущий код и делегирующий захват обученной политике, набирает 83.2%, и это преимущество объясняется выбором harness и языковой модели.

en.title: Hybrid LLM Agents Excel in Language-Conditioned Robot Manipulation
en.desc: This paper presents a new benchmark called SO-101 Bench for testing language-conditioned spatial manipulation tasks on low-cost robot arms. It shows that hybrid agents using large language models (LLMs) outperform traditional vision-language-action (VLA) policies in simulated environments, with consistent performance when tested on real hardware. The benchmark includes a variety of tasks and objects, allowing for comprehensive evaluation of different policies under controlled conditions. The findings indicate that integrating LLMs with learned policies significantly enhances performance in complex manipulation tasks.

zh.title: 混合LLM代理在机器人操作中的优势
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一个名为SO-101 Bench的模拟基准，用于评估语言条件下的空间操作，特别是在低成本机器人手臂上。研究表明，混合大型语言模型（LLM）代理在这些任务中表现优于传统的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略，并且在模拟和真实硬件上的排名一致性得到了验证。SO-101 Bench包含多个任务和对象，旨在测试机器人在复杂环境中的表现。结果显示，使用LLM代理的策略在执行语言条件任务时显著提高了成功率。

papers.title: ABF-Bench: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Blockchain Forensics
papers.abstract: Abstract ABF-Bench introduces an interactive, evidence-backed benchmark for blockchain fund tracing that evaluates adaptive agents against fixed tracers, revealing gaps in recall and overconfidence while enabling verifiable LLM agent training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Blockchain forensics is adversarial and open-ended: money launderers split, swap, and bridge funds, cut their trail at mixers or custodial services, and change tactics from one incident to the next. Investigators must keep adapting their tracing in response. Yet the immutability of public ledgers preserves every recorded movement in public view, making much of the investigation independently verifiable. We introduce ABF-Bench, an interactive benchmark that makes evidence-backed fund tracing a verifiable agent task, in which every claimed movement must cite ledger records the agent retrieved. A case-to-task pipeline builds well-posed tasks across ledgers: conservative rules halt tracing wherever the records leave a continuation unresolved, and each task's reference graph is the answer those rules determine. Built from real laundering activity, the tasks combine multi-hop transfers, DeFi exchanges, cross-chain round trips, custodial and mixer deposits, and address poisoning. We also propose the ABF agent harness, built around a working memory, and evaluate it alongside general-purpose agents and fixed-order tracers. The harness reaches 75% edge recall, against 47% for Codex with the same model and 10% for Claude Code, which loses recall to overconfidence: it cites records it left unretrieved. Compared with fixed-order tracers, the harness acquires evidence faster than the best of them early in the budget and recognizes undisclosed custodial services that they walk past (89% vs. 0%), with 98% fidelity. However, agents tend to stop early and lose recall on larger tasks, which holds their final recall below the best tracer. Beyond exposing these gaps, ABF-Bench opens blockchain forensics to LLM agents as a verifiable domain, where the verdicts that score agents also offer potential training signals.

papers.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
papers.abstract: Abstract Effective learning rate trajectories primarily drive weight-normalized training gains, motivating an affine inverse-square-root schedule that improves large-scale pretraining loss and robustness.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Weight-normalized (WN) training is emerging as a compelling alternative to conventional weight decay (WD), with recent studies reporting substantial pretraining loss gains. We show that these gains are driven primarily by the induced effective learning rate (ELR) trajectory rather than by normalization alone. Matching ELR trajectories largely collapses the training loss dynamics of WN and WD. Schedule design should therefore target ELR rather than the nominal learning rate (LR) alone. Building on this principle, we propose AIR (Affine Inverse-square-Root decay), which combines a theoretically derived 1/t decay with an affine adjustment to satisfy prescribed peak and terminal LRs over a finite training horizon. We further identify late-stage ELR scheduling as a key source of its gains, because a shared late schedule attenuates the effect of earlier LR choices. Experiments on 128 B-token Mixture-of-Experts pretraining demonstrate that AIR outperforms cosine and other candidate schedules in training loss, downstream performance, and hyperparameter robustness, reducing terminal training loss by approximately 0.01 relative to cosine at matched cumulative LR. Applying the same ELR trajectory to WD reproduces the corresponding training dynamics, showing that the benefits extend beyond fixed-norm training and establishing ELR as the principled scheduling object.

ru.title: Управляйте эффективным learning rate, а не номинальным
ru.desc: Статья показывает, что основной вклад в улучшение обучения при weight-normalized тренировке даёт не сама нормализация, а траектория эффективного learning rate (ELR). Совпадение ELR делает динамику функции потерь у WN и weight decay (WD) почти одинаковой, поэтому расписание нужно проектировать под ELR, а не под номинальный LR. На основе этого авторы предлагают расписание AIR, сочетающее теоретически выведенное затухание 1/t с аффинной коррекцией под заданные пиковый и финальный LR. Эксперименты на предобучении Mixture-of-Experts модели на 128B токенах показывают превосходство AIR над cosine по loss, downstream-метрикам и устойчивости к гиперпараметрам.

en.title: Optimize Training with Effective Learning Rate Scheduling
en.desc: This paper introduces a new learning rate schedule called AIR (Affine Inverse-square-Root decay) that enhances weight-normalized training in machine learning. The authors argue that the effective learning rate (ELR) trajectory is crucial for improving training loss and robustness, rather than just focusing on the nominal learning rate. By designing schedules that prioritize ELR, they demonstrate that AIR significantly outperforms traditional schedules like cosine in various training scenarios. Their experiments show that applying the same ELR trajectory to weight decay methods also yields similar training dynamics, highlighting the importance of ELR in optimizing training processes.

zh.title: 优化学习率，提升训练效果！
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了有效学习率轨迹对权重归一化训练效果的影响，提出了一种新的调度方法——仿射反平方根衰减（AIR）。研究表明，AIR能够显著改善大规模预训练的损失和鲁棒性，主要是通过优化有效学习率（ELR）轨迹来实现的。与传统的权重衰减（WD）相比，权重归一化（WN）训练在预训练损失上取得了显著的提升。实验结果显示，AIR在训练损失、下游性能和超参数鲁棒性方面优于余弦调度等其他候选调度。

papers.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
papers.abstract: Abstract Foundation-model training stages can be unified under a single likelihood-based algorithm that blends static data and reinforcement learning generations, improving efficiency and capability retention.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. We show that this algorithmic separation is not fundamental. By deriving suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, we place all of these stages under a single likelihood-based training algorithm, unified training. This perspective turns the foundation-model training lifecycle into a problem of choosing which data to train on, in what proportions, and when, with conventional staged training as a special case. We instantiate this framework in a unified training system that mixes static data and RL generations within a single trainer. Across controlled and real-world experiments, unified training improves the accuracy-compute tradeoff and task coverage while preserving broader capabilities, and provides a stronger starting point for continual learning. This work lays the groundwork for a unified science of foundation-model training, connecting mathematical principles, training infrastructure, and the development of model capabilities.

papers.title: Scaling Lean Theorem Proving for Real-World Code Verification
papers.abstract: Abstract EasyProver is a Lean proving system using recursive agents and asynchronous search that solves nearly all Putnam and IMO benchmark problems, while Aegis generates harder verification tasks from competitive programming to benchmark provers and support reinforcement learning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present EasyProver, a Lean proving system built from recursive agents with isolated contexts, asynchronous search, parallel tactic probing, and an elastic elaboration service. Using an off-the-shelf frontier model with no additional training, it proves 669/672 PutnamBench problems and all six IMO 2026 formalizations and resolves 597/600 NTP4VC verification conditions and all 189 VERINA tasks by proof or refutation. Because these benchmarks are close to saturation, we also introduce Aegis, which converts competitive programming problems into much harder verification tasks over real implementations. The pipeline writes safe Rust solutions, translates them into Lean with Aeneas, generates specifications, and labels each frozen statement with a kernel-checked proof or refutation. It produces 2,045 differentially validated Rust-Lean program pairs and 11,533 candidate specifications. Unlike hand-written benchmarks, these tasks carry implementation-level obligations from fixed-width arithmetic, explicit failure, generated loops, casts, and functionalized mutation. On a stratified sample of 2,000 statements, EasyProver proves 1,054 (52.7%) within a 30-minute budget per statement. The same tasks can also be used to benchmark other provers and as rewards for reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Abstract Holo4D guides video diffusion with reconstructed 3D trajectory scaffolds to synthesize novel-view videos while preserving geometry and motion.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Synthesizing a monocular video from a new camera trajectory requires preserving the observed scene geometry and motion while completing regions that become newly visible. Feed-forward 4D reconstructors recover the structure of the observed scene, whereas video diffusion models provide a generative prior for completing unseen content. We introduce Holo4D, a video reshooting framework that uses reconstructed 3D trajectories as a holistic source-view 4D scaffold. We project these trajectories into the requested views and encode their geometry and source appearance to guide a pretrained video diffusion model. Together with the source video and target cameras, the scaffold grounds generation in reconstructed observations while leaving unsupported regions to the generative prior. Experiments demonstrate the value of trajectory-based conditioning for camera control and novel-view synthesis. The framework accommodates different 4D reconstructors without retraining the video generator, allowing it to benefit from future advances in source reconstruction. More details can be found in our project page.

papers.title: After One-Click Video: The Inflow of Service-Type Content, the Failure of the Recommendation Pool Mechanism, and the BoLe System
papers.abstract: Abstract AI-generated video tools shift content production toward service-type material, unbalancing the industry and overwhelming recommendation systems, prompting a dual-judgment BoLe framework to protect work-type content.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small In September 2026, a new large language model was released. Soon after, a new way of making explainer videos became very popular: people asked the model to write a program, and the program produced the video. "One-click video" content then appeared in large amounts on many platforms. On the surface, this is a rise in creative power at the level of the individual. We argue that, at a deeper level, it changes the structure of the content industry. This judgment rests on two observations. First, this wave of content is service-type content. People watch it to meet a need, not to enjoy the content itself. The other kind is work-type content. AI makes both kinds faster to produce. But anyone can come in and make service-type content, while work-type content is limited by the number of people who have something to say. So the ratio between the two slowly becomes unbalanced. Second, free platforms choose content through layers of trial viewing, and this uses up user attention. The total amount of attention is fixed. The unbalanced ratio also dilutes good content. A simplified mathematical model shows that, as long as these conditions hold, the recommendation pool mechanism will fail once new content grows past a certain multiple. Based on this, we discuss one possible way out. Machines and entry rules judge whether service-type content passes the bar. Trusted people judge work-type content. We call this the BoLe system. At the end, we briefly imagine how the two kinds of content may develop from here.

ru.title: Видео по одному клику захлёстывает платформы, а ценный контент тонет
ru.desc: В статье рассматривается, как AI-инструменты для генерации видео (например, LLM, которая пишет программу для создания ролика) наводнили платформы контентом типа «услуга», то есть роликами, которые смотрят ради удовлетворения потребности, а не ради самого контента. Авторы показывают, что такой контент дешевле и быстрее производится, поэтому соотношение с контентом типа «работа» постепенно становится несбалансированным. Упрощённая математическая модель демонстрирует, что при фиксированном объёме внимания пользователей система рекомендаций перестаёт работать, когда объём нового контента превышает определённый порог. В качестве решения предлагается двойная схема оценки BoLe: машины и формальные правила отбирают контент типа «услуга», а проверенные люди оценивают контент типа «работа».

en.title: Balancing AI-Generated Content: The BoLe Framework
en.desc: This paper discusses the impact of AI-generated video tools on the content production industry, highlighting a shift towards service-type content that meets immediate needs rather than providing enjoyment. It introduces the BoLe framework, which aims to balance the production of service-type and work-type content by implementing dual judgment systems. The authors argue that the overwhelming amount of easily produced service-type content dilutes the quality of work-type content, leading to an imbalance in the industry. They propose a mathematical model to illustrate how recommendation systems may fail as the volume of new content increases, suggesting a need for structured evaluation of content types.

zh.title: 保护创作，平衡内容生态
zh.desc: 这篇论文讨论了AI生成视频工具对内容生产的影响，导致服务型内容的增加，进而影响了内容行业的结构。服务型内容是为了满足需求而观看的，而工作型内容则是由有独特见解的人创作的。随着AI技术的发展，生产这两种内容的速度都在加快，但服务型内容的生产门槛较低，导致两者之间的比例失衡。论文提出了一种双重判断的BoLe框架，以保护工作型内容，并探讨了未来内容发展的可能方向。

papers.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Pretrained raster-scan autoregressive image models can be adapted into flexible any-order generators via future-aware positional embeddings and an ordering curriculum, enabling inpainting and outpainting with minimal extra compute.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Autoregressive (AR) image generators are powerful in principle but inflexible in practice: training with a fixed raster-scan order hardcodes a single factorization of the image distribution into the model, leaving it unable to inpaint, outpaint, or edit at inference time. Existing solutions, including the modern discrete-diffusion family, train from scratch on a mixture of token orderings, paying roughly 3x the compute of standard raster-scan training; discrete diffusion further sacrifices compatibility with the AR inference ecosystem (KV caching, vLLM) by construction. We argue that this cost is unnecessary. A pretrained raster-scan AR model has already learned the joint distribution over image tokens; what it lacks is not knowledge but the ability to express that knowledge through non-sequential conditional pathways. We propose a recipe for adapting pretrained raster-scan models into any-order generators using two components: future-aware positional embeddings that resolve a target-position identifiability problem at negligible overhead, and an ordering curriculum that traces a stable optimization path from the pretrained solution to a good any-order basin. Applied to four base models across two architectures and two scales (LlamaGen-L/XL, RAR-L/XL), the recipe substantially outperforms MaskGIT on ImageNet inpainting (FID 6.21 vs. 10.44) and outpainting, is competitive with MAR-L, trades a 1.2-1.9 increase in class-conditional FID for this flexibility, and costs 13-33% additional compute beyond pretraining, while leaving the standard AR inference stack untouched. Inpainting, outpainting, and editing, our results suggest, need not be added to autoregressive image models. They can be unlocked from the ones that exist. Code is available at https://github.com/Ordered-AR/unlockedadaptation.

papers.title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract Matched interface representations significantly alter agent behavior despite identical executable capabilities, and targeted repair of interface-specific realization improves performance while reducing cost.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Language agents increasingly act through external tools and interactive environments, making the interface between the model and its executable capabilities part of the decision process. Model Context Protocol (MCP) and command-line interfaces (CLI) can expose the same semantic operations through markedly different model-facing representations. We study whether these representational differences change agent behavior when executable capabilities are matched. We introduce Matched Interface Comparison and Analysis (MICA), which renders MCP and CLI from a shared semantic action contract and routes decoded actions through the same runtime. Across six models and three interactive environments, matched interfaces produce substantial differences in task performance and interaction cost. These effects extend beyond surface validity to semantic action selection, failure pathways, and recovery. Matched-state probes localize sensitivity to capability presentation, realization, and feedback. Paired natural trajectories reveal structured divergence in 94.3% of 2,004 episodes and show that early differences propagate through subsequent interaction. This analysis identifies interface realization as a direct intervention boundary. We therefore introduce Decoupled Action Realization and Targeted Repair (DART), which preserves validated semantic commitments while repairing interface-specific realization. DART improves benchmark score in all six evaluated settings by up to 9.0 points and reduces MCP token cost in all three environments by up to 27.1k tokens per task. Together, these results establish interface representation as part of the closed-loop decision environment shaping agent behavior.

papers.title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
papers.abstract: Abstract Quantized small language model files in public registries can be non-functional due to uncalibrated quantization recipes, and screening plus calibration is recommended before release.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Developers download quantized large language models (LLMs) from public registries to run them locally. None of the registries we examined documented functional testing of their files. We tested all 305 eligible code-capable GGUF tags (the llama.cpp format) across 15 model lines in the official Ollama library, plus 22 popular Hugging Face community files. A 15-task code screen identified suspects, which we retested on all 164 HumanEval+ tasks. Seven official tags (2.3%) solved at most six of them. All were low-bit quantizations of models with at most four billion parameters. We rebuilt five suspect files from the original weights. All five registry files matched our uncalibrated rebuilds tensor for tensor, so none was corrupted. Exact reproducibility did not imply function. With the weights, toolchain and tensor mix held fixed, adding an importance matrix raised three Qwen2.5-Coder-3B builds from zero to 76-113 solved tasks. The same uncalibrated recipe left the smaller Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B functional, showing that the recipe alone does not predict failure. None of 66 sampled tags that passed the screen was non-functional. We release the audit data and the quantcheck tool and recommend screening low-bit tags before publication, then calibrating or withholding failures.

papers.title: FDSML: Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning with Parameter-Aware Triplet Loss
papers.abstract: Abstract Formula-driven supervised metric learning uses continuous generative parameters to train embeddings with parameter-aware triplet loss, improving synthetic pre-training for image retrieval and robustness.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Formula-Driven Supervised Learning (FDSL) enables vision pre-training without real images, but existing methods cast pre-training as classification on discretized labels, discarding continuity in the generative process. We propose Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning (FDSML), which derives relational supervision from image-generation parameters beyond discrete class labels. FDSML combines FineFractalDB, our refined fractal dataset with higher intra-class variation and more stable structures, with a Parameter-Aware Triplet (PA-Triplet) Loss that assigns positives and negatives according to distances in the underlying Iterated Function System parameter space. This objective trains embeddings to respect parameter-derived relative similarity orderings. Experiments show that FDSML improves transferability to image retrieval while remaining competitive on downstream classification and improving robustness under several corruption settings. On ResNet-50, Recall@1 improves from 65.6% to 74.0% on Stanford Online Products and from 56.2% to 78.4% on Stanford Cars over FDSL pre-training. These results suggest that parameter-derived relational supervision provides a stronger synthetic pre-training signal than label-based classification for transfer beyond recognition.

papers.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
papers.abstract: Abstract The study introduces EPSBench to evaluate AI agents in forecasting quarterly earnings by linking financial evidence to income-statement drivers and comparing model predictions to analyst consensus.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Quarterly earnings forecasting requires an agent to connect financial evidence to the income-statement line items that produce a company's reported earnings. We introduce EPSBench, a benchmark for studying this ability across 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies. Agents read a fixed collection of filings, earnings-call transcripts, and news, then estimate company-specific income-statement drivers with cited evidence. A shared accounting calculator converts these estimates into GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS), providing a common basis for comparing forecast assumptions. We evaluate six models under a common harness, assessing point forecast error relative to date-matched analyst consensus and checking whether their prediction intervals achieve the stated coverage. Three models show no detectable paired difference in point forecast error from consensus, and three have higher error. Across all six models, nominal 80% intervals contain reported EPS in only 37--70% of runs that return an interval, and most misses fall above the upper bound because the forecasts run low. The driver records trace most of the error gap between models to operating-income estimates.

papers.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Abstract WISD improves reasoning models by contrasting them with weaker quantized or pruned versions to generate training signals without privileged data.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Self-distillation offers a way to improve reasoning models when a suitable external teacher is unavailable. However, common approaches rely on privileged information to construct a stronger self-teacher, limiting their use when only unlabeled prompts are available. In this paper, we introduce Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation (WISD), which instead constructs a weaker counterpart of the original model and uses the contrast between the two as a training signal without requiring privileged information. We explore two ways to construct the weaker model: low-bit quantization and magnitude pruning. We evaluate WISD across diverse architectures and scales on mathematical and coding reasoning tasks. Across these benchmarks, quantization and pruning improve average accuracy over the original models by 4.0 and 5.5 percentage points, respectively, achieving state-of-the-art performance even without privileged information. Notably, pruning raises Qwen3.5-4B's accuracy from 57.7% to 70.5% on HMMT 2025 and from 39.1% to 56.7% on LiveCodeBench v6. Quantization raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's accuracy from 68.5% to 74.6% and from 61.8% to 69.5% on the same benchmarks, respectively. These results establish WISD as a novel and effective self-distillation framework for large reasoning models.
